newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam eyes individual investors with T-note sale.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam eyes individual investors with T-note sale.

text.p: Vietnam, seeking capital to plug a state budget gap, will issue new two-year domestic Treasury notes from Saturday, a finance ministry official said on Friday.

The official told Reuters the notes would be available in denominations of 100,000 dong ($8.94) and Vietnamese individuals, resident foreigners and local social organisations would be invited to subscribe.
He said the State Treasury was hoping to raise up to 5,000 billion dong ($447.5 million) through the sale. Annual interest will be at 14 percent.
State dailies said a 13 percent rate would be paid on investments of more than one year but less than two.

Vietnam's budget deficit in 1996 has not been disclosed, but in 1995 it reached a level which Hanoi said was equivalent to 4.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) but which the International Monetary Fund put at 1.7 percent of GDP.
In recent years the government has stepped up efforts to tap both domestic and foreign capital to finance the budget and sustain economic growth, running at an annual rate of more than nine percent.

The Treasury began issuing notes in 1992 and auctioned its first bills in 1995, but the authorities are holding off on plans to test Vietnam's credit rating on world markets with an international bond debut.
